title: Trace embeddings to metric bridge and anomaly stitcher
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Motivation: Current burn-rate and anomaly alerts trigger noisy paging because signal correlation across traces, metrics, and logs is shallow. On-call spends time triaging multiple independent alerts that are actually the same underlying behavioral shift (e.g., upstream kv cache churn -> 95th latency increase -> increased error retries).

Goal: Build a lightweight pipeline that converts sampled trace spans into compact embeddings, joins them with time-series metric windows, and synthesizes 'stitch events' that group cross-signal anomalies. The stitched events will be used by alerting rules to reduce duplicate pages and to attach representative trace examples to SLO incident pages for faster diagnosis.

Scope:
- Sidecar/ingester component that consumes trace spans (odp/jaeger) and produces fixed-size embeddings (small transformer or graph-based embedder tuned for span semantics).
- Metric joiner that aligns embedding footprints with metric windows (latency/error histograms, percentiles, QPS) and computes similarity clusters for a short timespan (1m–15m windows).
- Anomaly stitcher service that outputs correlated incidents with metadata: cluster score, representative trace id, top contributing metrics, and suggested runbook hints.
- Integration points: burn-rate alerting policies (allow alert gating if stitch score > threshold), SLO incident pages (show representative trace & cluster summary), and Console incident feed.

Non-goals: Full replacement of existing SLI/SLO rules, long-term storage of embeddings (we keep only short-lived, sliding-window caches), and complex model training infra (use small, self-contained embedder that can be packaged with the sidecar).

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Embeddings vs heuristics: embeddings provide semantic similarity beyond exact tag matching (e.g., same stacktrace shape even with different error messages). Cost: modest CPU/GPU for embedding; mitigate by sampling (configurable rate) and lightweight models.
- Window alignment: choose 1m windows for low-latency detection, 5–15m for cluster stabilization. A multi-window approach reduces false positives but increases compute; start with 1/5m dual windows.
- Gating policy: burn-rate alerts may be allowed to auto-suppress paging if stitch score is high and cluster size > N. This reduces pages for mass-impact non-prod blips but must be conservative for high-severity errors.

Alternatives evaluated:
- Using raw span hashes + top-k tag matching: cheaper but brittle for de novo failures.
- Full ML anomaly detection on metrics alone: ignores trace-level fingerprints that help triage root cause quickly.

Success metrics:
- 30% reduction in duplicate pages for correlated events within first 3 months in canary tenants.
- Median time-to-first-diagnostic (time from page to representative trace being available) reduced by 40%.
- False suppression rate < 1% for high-severity SLO failures (safety guard).
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar can ingest sampled spans and produce embeddings at configured sampling rates (0.1%–5%) for canary workload
Metric joiner aligns embeddings with metric windows and produces correlated cluster events within 90s of window end
Stitcher outputs JSON incidents with representative_trace_id, cluster_score, contributing_metrics list, and runbook_hint tag
Burn-rate alerting can optionally use stitcher output to gate paging (feature flag + conservative defaults)
Console SLO incident page displays representative trace and cluster summary when stitch metadata exists
Performance: sidecar additional CPU < 10% on typical prod instance (at default sampling), memory increase < 200MB
Operational: monitoring dashboards for embedding latency, cluster false-positive rate, and gating decisions are available in Console
comments: 2026-02-21 - Avery Chen: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Trace-Embedding-Bridge. Agreed to prototype embedding model with lightweight transformer (150k params) and fall back to LSH hashing if performance unacceptable.

2026-02-28 - Leah Martinez: POC sidecar code is in draft branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/428. Initial embedder (onnx) runs at ~120ms/span on c5.large; we need to optimize to sub-50ms for target sampling. Next steps: quantize model and evaluate cpu vectorized inference path.

2026-03-04 - Design review (PM/Eng/SRE): Decided on dual-window approach (1m + 5m) and gating safety: never suppress paging for SLO error-rate breaches above critical threshold (customer_impact = high). Added requirement to record suppression decisions in audit log.

2026-03-08 - SRE feedback from Maya Kapoor: Ensure stitcher has deterministic cluster ids for de-duping and that representative trace selection prefers high-span-count traces for richer diagnostics. Also requested a kill-switch for auto-suppress in each region.
2026-03-09 - Leah Martinez: Integrated basic cluster scoring and added telemetry counters. Running canary in dev-tier tomorrow across three services (console, runtime, api-gateway).

2026-03-10 - QA: Found a race where metric windows and span ingestion offsets cause ~30s delay in cluster availability. Proposed fix: use watermark-based window advance tied to metric ingestion rather than wall-clock. Added task ENG-559124 to track fix.
